findings.title: SQL Injection via req.query.q in search function
findings.description: The search function concatenates user input directly into a SQL query string, allowing SQL injection.
findings.evidence: const term = req.query.q; return db.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + term + "'");
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements instead of string concatenation.

judge.reason: Model-generated code shows SQL injection; needs verification in actual codebase.

findings.title: SQL Injection via String Concatenation
findings.description: User-supplied input is directly concatenated into a SQL query string, allowing for SQL injection attacks that could lead to unauthorized data access, modification, or deletion.
findings.evidence: return db.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + term + "'");
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements. For example: db.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = $1", [term]);

judge.reason: Direct string concatenation in SQL query leads to SQL injection vulnerability.

findings.title: Command Injection via req.query.tool in childProcess.exec
findings.description: The runTool function takes a tool parameter from user input and passes it directly to childProcess.exec() without sanitization, allowing arbitrary command execution.
findings.evidence: export function runTool(req) { const tool = req.query.tool; return childProcess.exec("tool " + tool); }
findings.remediation: Avoid using exec with user input. Use spawn with argument array or validate/sanitize input strictly.

judge.reason: Model-generated code shows command injection; possible hallucination, needs verification.

findings.title: Command Injection via req.query.host in exec
findings.description: The /tools/ping endpoint uses exec with a template string containing the host parameter, leading to command injection.
findings.evidence: router.get("/tools/ping", (req, res) => { exec(`echo ${String(req.query.host ?? "localhost")}`, () => undefined); res.json({ queued: true }); });
findings.remediation: Use execFile or spawn with argument array. Avoid using shell execution with user input.

judge.reason: Model-generated command injection; needs verification.

findings.title: Shell execution may include user-controlled input
findings.description: Hermsec's offline heuristic scanner found a risky source pattern.
findings.evidence: src/routes/search.js:19 exec(`echo ${String(req.query.host ?? "localhost")}`, () => undefined);
findings.remediation: Use fixed argv arrays and validate user-controlled values before execution.

judge.reason: Direct interpolation of user-controlled query parameter into shell command without sanitization.

findings.title: Debug endpoint exposes token hash
findings.description: The /debug-token endpoint exposes an MD5 hash of the hardcoded token, which could be used to brute-force the token or leak information. Debug endpoints should be disabled in production.
findings.evidence:
File src/routes/search.js lines 30-33: router.get("/debug-token", (req, res) => { const name = String(req.query.name ?? "fixture-user"); const digest = crypto.createHash("md5").update(fakeFixtureToken).digest("hex"); res.send(`

${name}

${digest}

`); });
findings.remediation: Remove or restrict the /debug-token endpoint in production. Avoid using weak hashing algorithms like MD5.

judge.reason: Debug endpoint publicly exposes a token hash using weak MD5; remains a security concern even if token is a test fixture.
